descriptor.title: A competitor recruited our sales team
descriptor.introduction: Can a competitor hire our sales team and use its files? A fictional business decision with a reviewed action document.

strategies.title: Advice tested against business and legal risks
strategies.input_summary: Fictional Baylight Analytics employs six Massachusetts sales staff. Three resign for a competitor on September 18, 2026. Their 2023 agreements include confidentiality clauses and a customer nonsolicitation clause; no employee noncompetition covenant is supplied. A log shows one employee downloaded a 400-row customer pricing file two days before departure, but downloads also occurred during normal sales work. Baylight has not found evidence of competitor use or customer diversion. The file combines public customer names with nonpublic renewal dates and individually negotiated pricing. HR wants to threaten immediate litigation against the competitor and tell all customers the departing staff stole trade secrets.
assumptions: All business facts and organizations in this scenario are fictional.
Missing facts must remain unresolved rather than assumed favorable.

revised.response_text:
## Recommendation
Preserve evidence and investigate access, retention and actual use before accusing anyone of theft. Request return or deletion of company confidential information through a measured counsel letter, while preserving litigation evidence and allowing lawful employment. Assess the precise nonsolicitation language separately; do not manufacture a noncompete that the agreements do not contain.

## Risks
The pricing compilation may qualify for protection only if the statutory elements and reasonable secrecy measures are supported. Public names alone do not establish a secret; nonpublic pricing and renewal data may have different significance. A legitimate work download is an adverse explanation that must be tested. Section 24L is not a general prohibition on employee mobility and does not decide every confidentiality or nonsolicitation dispute.

## Options
A confidential preservation and return request can stop avoidable dissemination without prematurely alleging theft. A negotiated information firewall at the competitor may help if supported by evidence and workable controls. Emergency relief should be considered only after identifying protected material, wrongful conduct, urgency and proportionate relief; it may fail if the only evidence is ordinary access.

## Next Steps
IT should preserve audit logs and relevant devices without accessing personal accounts unlawfully. Legal should map each disputed file to secrecy controls, authorized access and observed activity. HR should collect signed agreements and onboarding/exit notices. Sales should monitor factual account developments without disparaging former employees. Counsel should approve any demand or court filing.

## Secondary Deliverable
**Preservation and return request — draft**
We understand that former Baylight employees have joined your business. Baylight does not object to lawful employment or competition. Its review has identified downloads of company pricing materials near departure; we are investigating their context and do not represent that misuse has been established. Please preserve potentially relevant records and take reasonable steps to prevent any Baylight confidential material from entering your systems or being used. Through counsel, please coordinate an evidence-preserving review and return or secure quarantine of any identified Baylight material. Do not delete potentially relevant evidence before an agreed preservation protocol. We propose discussing a narrowly tailored information firewall. This request does not seek competitors’ independent work or public information.

Massachusetts trade-secret protection depends on statutory secrecy/value and reasonable protective measures, with misappropriation requiring more than lawful recruitment.
